Thanks for the heads up, Sarah — we've got the alert and are triaging. Quick summary from the on-call team:

- Observed a rapid increase in client retries starting ~08:03 PT; concurrent active connections spiked ~3x.
- Syndicated 5xx responses originating from model-invoke proxies under heavy queuing and timeouts, plus 429s emitted from the gateway when internal throttles tripped.
- We've pulled an initial log bundle (attached).

Immediate actions in progress:
- Rishi and the SREs are running emergency scale-up of dedicated inference pool and temporarily raising per-model concurrency caps.
- Applying call-level rate-limits and rejecting obvious retry loops from identical client IPs.
- Asking Acme to hold aggressive client-side retries for the next 15 minutes while we stabilize.

Subject: Re: Production errors: 5xx/429 spikes impacting checkout (urgent)

Update / quick RCA and actions performed:

Root cause (summary):
- A client-side SDK change rolled out by Acme earlier that morning removed exponential backoff for a subset of retries and changed retry window semantics. This produced a concentrated retry storm against the inference gateway.
- Our autoscaler, tuned for average load, reacted slowly to the rapid ramp; scale-up lag + enqueue limits caused the proxy layer to return 5xx on timeouts and 429 when queue depth exceeded configured thresholds.
- A downstream throttling rule (conservative default per-tenant qps) combined with identical retry fingerprints amplified the effect.

Mitigations applied (08:35 - 13:30 PT):
- Emergency scale: increased dedicated pool by +40% and added temporary hot standby nodes (completed 08:50).
- Applied a short-term adaptive ingress rate-limit (per-IP + per-tenant) to cap retry amplification.
- Tuned gateway queue depth and extended request timeouts for inference proxies to avoid cascade failures.
- Coordinated with Acme to push a client rollback for the retry change; they paused aggressive retries at 09:05.

Post-incident observations:
- Error rates returned to baseline by ~09:30 once both client-side retry pause and our emergency scaling were active.
- We saw a secondary smaller spike at 11:40 when autoscaler tested a scale-down cycle; that was capped by updated cooldown rules.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Update alerting thresholds to include correlated 429+5xx simultaneous anomaly detection (owner: Rishi, ETA: 2026-03-24).
- Add a retry-storm runbook and mandatory playbook steps for customer-facing teams (owner: Jonas, ETA: 2026-03-23).
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-up latency and add proactive pre-warm for scheduled merchant events (owner: Tessa, ETA: 2026-04-07).
- SLO tuning: adjust alert burn-rate window vs short-term bursts; add a 1m and 15m paired alert (owner: Laura, ETA: 2026-03-31).
- Postmortem doc and customer-facing summary (owner: Marissa, ETA: 2026-03-18 EOD).

Folks — final post-incident update and consolidated action items. Thanks to the on-call+SREs for the fast containment. TL;DR: retry storm triggered by client SDK change + autoscaler lag -> 5xx/429 spike -> mitigated by emergency scale and rate-limits.

Summary of changes we will make (follow-ups):
- Runbook: I drafted an initial retry-storm runbook and pushed to docs (see link). The runbook includes immediate user-facing scripts (rate-limit toggles, emergency scaling commands, circuit-breaker config). Attachment: runbook-draft-20260318.md
- Alerts: Rishi's team will add composite alerts that correlate 429 and 5xx with concurrent inflight connection spikes. We'll also add a short burn-rate alarm for 1m spike detection.
- Autoscaler: Tessa's team will reduce scale-up window and add a pre-warm hook for large tenant windows; we will run a chaos test next week to validate.
- Customer comms: Marissa will finalize the customer-facing note and next steps; draft sent to Acme (HubSpot link below).
